newsitem.title: INDIA: India's SEBI asks for daily data on short-sales.
newsitem.headline: India's SEBI asks for daily data on short-sales.

text.p: Market regulator the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) on Thursday said all Indian exchanges must ask member brokers to submit their scrip-wise net short sales positions at the end of the day.
SEBI said in a statement stock exchanges were being asked to implement this from November 29.
SEBI has defined short sales as the selling of shares without having physical possession unless it is for squaring-up of an earlier purchase in the same settlement and in the same stock exchange.
This information would be required for 60 actively traded stocks. Stock exchanges were expected to compile these scrip-wise positions and make them public by the next day.
SEBI said the move was an "interim measure" and a committee had been set up to formulate more norms on short-selling and stock lending.
